chunk_findings.detail: The new guard treats every failed `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` as “not a git repository” and tells the user to `git init`. That command also exits non-zero when the directory already is a repository but git refuses it, for example a tree owned by another user (`fatal: detected dubious ownership in repository`, exit 128), a `safe.directory` rejection, or a permissions error on `.git`. Given that input, onboard status/preflight/verify returns exit 1 with “run `git init` there first” and never reaches the real probe, so a valid repo is misdiagnosed and the suggested fix is wrong (and `git init` on that tree is not what they need).

chunk_findings.detail: The stated fix for B-onb-cap-msg never lands: this change only renames the unused CLI status from `code` to `_code` and leaves every import message path untouched. Repro from the bug still fails the same way: a repo with a TODO.md of 300 phases × 100 checkbox tasks, `ddflow init`, then `ddflow import` (or `import --max-tasks 50`) still prints REFUSING (cap 200) followed by “Nothing to import” and “Nothing recognisable was found… not necessarily wrong”, even though the file was recognised. Ignoring the exit code also means a non-zero refusal is treated as a pass as long as those two strings are absent from the captured text.

chunk_findings.detail: A bare repo has no `.git` entry, so a failed `rev-parse` (dubious ownership, permissions, corrupt gitdir) makes the parent walk return True and the caller tell the user to `git init`. Example: `git init --bare /tmp/bare.git`, then `rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` exits non-zero with `fatal: detected dubious ownership in repository`. Old code left that case alone because the message is not `not a git repository`; the new code treats it as “not a repository.” The refusal test only covers a non-bare tree that already has `.git`.
